subject: Post-demo: procurement & purchasing path (PO vs card) — next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + procurement questions

Jordan — thanks again for a great demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can line up procurement: 

- Redwood fit: You confirmed primary use is real-time commerce chat for checkout flows (low-latency, predictable throughput on peak sale events).
- Preferred deployment: you mentioned interest in Dedicated for predictable performance but also asked about a hosted pilot for the initial sprint.
- Procurement & purchasing path questions: do you operate on Purchase Order (PO) terms through central procurement, or is a corporate card the usual route for pilots under $10k? Also — any preference for procuring via AWS Marketplace (paperwork + consolidated billing) vs direct Redwood invoicing?

Next steps I propose: I can send a short one-pager that maps hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) to procurement flows (card, PO, marketplace) and recommended pricing packaging (commits vs on-demand) tailored to your volume profile. Will also attach a simplified pricing sheet and a one-page MSA summary for your legal/procurement team to review.

Can you confirm: primary procurement contact and whether a PO is required to start a multi-month pilot?

Thanks — Soo

--
Soojin Lee

Thanks, Soo — quick answers from procurement: 

- For pilots under $15k our team can usually approve via corporate card. Anything above that typically needs a PO and legal review.
- Preferred is a PO for multi-quarter commitments; card for short-term pilots.
- We prefer marketplace purchases for vendor consolidation (AWS Marketplace) but procurement will accept direct invoicing if we have an approved SOW + MSA.

Primary procurement contact is Taylor Hsu (cc'd). Taylor — I expect we'll run a 6–8 week pilot covering checkout conversational flows; estimated committed spend TBD after you send the pricing mapping.

Jordan
Director, Product
Nimbus Retail
jordan.price@nimbusretail.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Taylor Hsu <taylor.hsu@nimbusretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + procurement questions

Appreciate the clarity, Jordan. TL;DR for procurement: 

- Pilot recommendation: Hosted (on-demand) for the first 4–8 weeks to reduce procurement friction — card ok if spend < $15k.
- If you want predictable latency for peak events we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) with a 12-month commit; procurement usually prefers PO for commits.
- AWS Marketplace: good option if you want consolidated billing and faster procurement; we can publish an offering and provide marketplace pricing that maps to our direct pricing.

I've attached a one-page mapping (see Redwood_Simplified_Pricing_v1.pdf) that shows example spend tiers and recommended packaging. Key callouts: 
- Pilot (hosted, on-demand): quick to spin up, minimal contract — good for initial validation.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): lower unit cost at scale but requires commit/PO and lead time to reserve capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated data — procurement + security will need the full MSA and implementation SOW.

Marcus — tagging you for suggested draft pricing guidance for a 6–8 week pilot vs a 12-month commit that we can present to Taylor and legal. Laura — can you confirm if our AWS Marketplace team can expedite listing prep if they choose that path?

Soo
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@nimbusretail.com>, Taylor Hsu <taylor.hsu@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 14:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + procurement questions

Soojin / team — draft guidance inline: 

- 6–8 week pilot (Hosted, on-demand): suggest a capped billing estimate of $8k–$12k depending on qps distribution; offer a one-month extension at a 10% discounted on-demand rate if they commit within pilot. No PO required under $15k; card preferred.
- 12-month Dedicated commit: three tier commit bands with ~20–35% unit-cost savings vs on-demand depending on commit size. PO + signed SOW required. Lead time to reserve capacity: ~3–6 weeks.
- Marketplace route: if Nimbus prefers AWS Marketplace, we can mirror direct pricing but the contract flow is through Marketplace (good for corporate consolidation). Time to publish: ~2–3 weeks with our AWS marketplace specialist.

I'll prepare a short pricing table for the pilot vs commit and drop into the Drive link Soo shared.

—Marcus
Head of Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

2) If we pick Hosted on-demand via card and later convert to Dedicated commit, will you provide any credit for pilot spend toward the commit?

If you can confirm those two points I can open the PO request (if we go commit) or approve the card spend for the pilot. Looking forward to the pricing table and the MSA summary for legal.
